name: veterinary_clinic_system_055_amendment_chain_repair
instruction: The clinic's medical-record policy treats locked visit notes as immutable: after a note is locked, any change must be made by appending a new linked amendment record, never by editing the original. As of the episode date, you must identify every visit record that has been tampered with and repair its chain. A tampered record is a locked visit_records row (locked_at is non-null) whose updated_at timestamp is later than its locked_at timestamp — this is the only signal; the audit_log does not contain separate edit events for these notes. For each tampered original: leave the original untouched; append a new visit_records amendment row with the same patient_id, provider_id, location_id, and weight_kg; visit_date set to the episode date; subjective 'Amendment of <YYYY-MM-DD of original visit_date> note: record was modified after locking; content under review.'; objective 'Original weight: <weight_kg> kg.'; assessment 'Amendment pending clinical review.'; plan 'Original note quarantined for compliance.'; problems []; locked_at null; amends set to the original's id as a string; and batch set to the episode batch_code. Do not create a duplicate amendment for the same original id in the same episode (re-runs must be idempotent). Also write one ops_reports row report='amendment_chain' for this batch with tampered_count, amendment_count, unlocked_count, and location_breakdown (an object mapping each location_id to the number of tampered notes at that location). If an amendment_chain report already exists for this batch, overwrite it so the report stays current. Nothing outside visit_records and ops_reports may be changed.
_max_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.
_par_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.

success_criteria.summary: From seed: 344 visit_records rows have locked_at set and updated_at > locked_at (string compare). They each get exactly one new visit_records amendment with amends=<original id> and batch=<batch>. 27 original rows have locked_at null and must not be amended. The original 371 seed rows must remain byte-identical. Exactly one ops_reports row report='amendment_chain' for this batch with tampered_count=344, amendment_count=344, unlocked_count=27, and location_breakdown={'1':116,'2':112,'3':116}. Dual-path counts (Python vs SQL) must agree.

checks.expect: exactly 344 new amendment rows keyed by (amends, batch); originals unchanged
tampered count and per-location counts recomputed independently via SQL and Python; both agree with the amendment rows and the ops_reports summary

hazards: visit_records id=371 has locked_at=null and an empty plan; it is an incomplete note but not a tampered locked note. A solution that conflates 'incomplete' with 'tampered' and appends an amendment for it over-produces and fails the seed row count and field checks.

visit_records id=27, 57, 86, 90, 114 are also unlocked (locked_at null) and must not receive an amendment. Over-broad 'append for all visit records' or 'append for all records without a problems list' would fail the new-row count.

The audit_log (4 rows: TRANSFER_COMPLETED target patients, OWNER_MERGE, CS_LOG_APPENDED, ESTIMATE_CONVERTED) contains no visit_records edit events, so a solution that tries to derive the tampered set from audit_log will find nothing and miss all 344 tampered rows.

The timestamp comparison must be a string compare of ISO 8601 values (updated_at > locked_at), not datetime parsing or simple locked_at presence; in this seed all 344 locked rows are tampered, but a solution that ignores updated_at entirely cannot survive a seed where a record was locked and never edited.
Original seed rows must remain byte-identical. A solution that edits an original to set amends or clear locked_at is a direct violation of the immutability rule and fails the seed canary check.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 expands the v1 single-append rule into a chain-repair workflow with a grouped ops_reports summary and dual-path (SQL vs Python) forensic counting. It adds an explicit audit_log-canary hazard and an incomplete-note decoy (visit_records id=371) to distinguish tampering from documentation incompleteness.
